newsitem.title: UK: Gold shuffles in range, shrugs off stock market.
newsitem.headline: Gold shuffles in range, shrugs off stock market.

text.p: Gold prices stagnated in a narrow band on Tuesday with the spotlight firmly turned to the ups and downs in the stock market, dealers said.
Bullion dealers had little response to an early surge, and a subsequent sharp decline in U.S. and European stocks.
"There was a little push up this morning...But then people ran out of ideas," a dealer said.
Bullion closed slightly firmer at $383.55 an ounce, compared to Monday's $382.80 London close.
But prices appeared to have limited upside scope despite breaking above a three-week-old downtrend line, analysts said.
"Initial support at $382 should hold gold now and downside for silver and platinum looks slim near term," said technical analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge.
"But none of these precious metals looks likely to enjoy any corrective gains worth talking about," she added.
Trading volumes were thin early in the day with big players concentrating on surging stocks following Wall Street's record highs on Monday, dealers said.
Key European and U.S. bourses then tumbled following midday comments by a senior Fed official which raised fresh worries about U.S. interest rates.
The bullion market was still in limbo ahead of a decision by the International Monetary Fund on a controversial plan to sell five million ounces of gold to finance aid to poor countries.
International monetary sources said the IMF, due to resume discussion on Wednesday, was having trouble reaching agreement.
"The IMF is teasing us," a dealer said. The protracted debate has undermined prices in recent days, but dealers expect that a decision could lead to a brisk, if short-term, rally.
The white industrial metals were slightly firmer, but dealers said they should have done better considering the stock market's recent strong performance.
Palladium fixed at a three-year low of $121.00 an ounce after eroding steadily in recent weeks, and was vulnerable to further losses, dealers said.
It closed at $121.75, up $0.75 from Monday's London finish, while platinum ended up $0.90 at $388.50.
Silver closed just two cents higher from Monday's London close at $5.07 an ounce, dragged down by sluggishness in gold and weakness in the other white metals platinum and palladium.
